# Incident Report — MTA 2024-07-30 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 172.16.1.66 |
| MAC address | 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-SKBR25F (domain: wiresharkworkshop.online) |
| Logged-in Windows user | ccollier |
| Domain controller (LAN) | 172.16.1.4 (WIRESHARK-WS-DC) |

Hostname and MAC confirmed via NBNS/Kerberos traffic (host authenticates to the DC as `DESKTOP-SKBR25F$` and user `ccollier` via Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ). Windows version and AV product are further corroborated by the malware's own beacon telemetry (below).

## Malware Family

**STRRAT** — a Java-based remote access trojan. Attribution is **signature-confirmed**, not inferred from behavior: the C2 beacon transmits the literal ASCII string `STRRAT` in plaintext on every check-in, e.g.:

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender||1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<uptime> Sec
```

This pipe-delimited beacon (STRRAT protocol version 1.6) also self-reports the victim ID (`1BE8292C`), hostname, username, OS build, AV product, and country — all consistent with the observed environment. Beaconing is sent every ~5 seconds over a raw (non-TLS) TCP socket on a non-standard port, matching STRRAT's known unencrypted "ping" C2 protocol.

**Infection timeline:**
1. t=63.96s: DNS resolves `github.com` and `repo1.maven.org`
2. t=64.05s–64.83s: connections to `github.com` (140.82.113.3) and `objects.githubusercontent.com` (185.199.110.133) over TLS — likely the STRRAT jar/dropper stage
3. t=68.0s: 8.8 MB TLS download from `repo1.maven.org` (199.232.196.209) in 5.8 seconds — consistent with retrieval of a bundled Java runtime (STRRAT commonly ships/fetches a JRE to run on hosts without Java)
4. t=76.99s: first raw TCP connection to the C2, 141.98.10.79:12132 — persists for the rest of the capture (through t=585.66s, pcap end)
5. t=77.87s: DNS/HTTP lookup of `ip-api.com` (208.95.112.1) — geo-IP self-check, whose result ("US:United States") is echoed in every subsequent beacon
6. t=340.38s: DNS query for `javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com` — consistent with STRRAT's Java-update/runtime-check behavior

All content transferred over TLS (GitHub/maven stages) could not be inspected — no file names or hashes were recoverable from ciphertext, and no cleartext HTTP file transfers containing malware payloads were observed in this capture.

## Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control:**
- `141.98.10.79:12132` (TCP, plaintext STRRAT ping protocol) — active C2, single persistent stream (tcp.stream 0), 83 total packets exchanged, beacon interval ~5s

**Supporting/staging infrastructure observed in traffic (delivery chain, TLS-encrypted — domains only, no recoverable payload):**
- `github.com` (140.82.113.3)
- `objects.githubusercontent.com` (185.199.110.133)
- `repo1.maven.org` (199.232.196.209) — 8.8 MB payload transfer
- `ip-api.com` (208.95.112.1) — plaintext HTTP `GET /json/`, victim geolocation lookup used by the malware
- `javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com` (23.194.164.136) — Java runtime check consistent with STRRAT behavior

**Malicious URLs:** none recoverable — the initial-access and staging traffic is entirely TLS-encrypted; the only cleartext HTTP requests observed (`www.msftconnecttest.com/connecttest.txt`, `ip-api.com/json/`) are benign/legitimate.

**Transferred files / hashes:** **none recoverable.** No cleartext file transfer (HTTP, SMB with exfil, etc.) carrying an executable or document payload was present in the capture; all suspected payload delivery occurred over TLS, so no SHA256 can be grounded in this evidence. Do not treat any hash as confirmed unless independently obtained (e.g., from EDR/host forensics).

**STRRAT beacon fields (host self-report, corroborating victim identity):**
- Victim ID: `1BE8292C`
- OS: Microsoft Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit
- AV: Windows Defender
- STRRAT client version: 1.6
- Reported country: US (United States)
